newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Sears breaks-itself up, Strong quits.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Sears breaks-itself up, Strong quits.

text.p: British stores group Sears Plc on Tuesday announced the break-up of its retail empire, including the demerger of upmarket department store Selfridges, to try to improve returns for its long-suffering shareholders.

Sears unveiled the long-awaited shake-up as it announced 1996 annual results and the sale of its Freemans mail order business to Littlewoods LWD.CN for 367.5 million pounds ($597 million), along with plans to hand the proceeds to shareholders.

The retailer, which has been hard hit by long-running losses from its shoe business, also announced the departure of its beleaguered chief executive Liam Strong, who had come under attack for failing to turn the around the group's performance after five years in the job.
Sears's restructuring aims to ditch its loss-hit British Shoe Corporation, leaving women and children wear chains plus the demerged Selfridges, its star earner.
The announcement ended months of speculation about a break-up and the fate of Strong, whose failure to revive the business had tried the patience of institutional shareholders.
He was hired to inject new life into Sears' far flung retail empire, but his actions failed to revive the business, despite a retail boom.
Chairman Sir Bob Reid said the restructuring would secure Sears' future.
"We've pruned the roses, when you prune the roses you get good blooms, super growth," he told Reuters by telephone.
Sears has appointed David James as executive chairman of BSC to oversee its rationalisation.

James, described as an expert in dealing with rescue situations, would look at each of the shoe businesses and see what their value was in the open market, look at the advantages of holding on to them, or selling them.
Reid said it was too early to say what the cost might be to Sears of the rationalisation. "We would deal with the provisions when we've actually gone through the shoe businesses one by one."
He declined to make any predictions on job cuts which might follow the restructuring.

He said Sears wanted to complete the rationalisation by the end of this year. There were several companies interested in BSC, he said, including U.S. shoe retailers Nine West Group and Payless Shoesource.
Reid said the Selfridges demerger would go ahead towards the middle of next year and described recent estimates valuing Selfridges' at around 600 million pounds as "conservative."
"We're looking for a lot more than that," he told Reuters, "It's a way above 600 million."
Sears reported annual pre-tax profits before exceptional charges of 88.9 million pounds against 70.8 million the previous year, while maintaining its dividend at 3.95 pence per share.
The group's shares stood one pence higher at 78.5 pence.
